name: MasTec, Inc.
moat_justification: Weak-moderate. Scale, national footprint, bonding capacity, utility/telecom incumbency and a record $21.4B 18-month backlog give real bidding advantages on large programs, but the work is competitively bid, labor- and fleet-based, with thin margins and no durable pricing power: fundamentals.json ROE ran 12.9% (2021), 1.2% (2022), -1.8% (2023), 5.6% (2024), 12.2% (2025) — at or below the cost of capital through most of the cycle (management noted on the Q4 2025 call that ROIC met its WACC hurdle in 2025 for the first time since 2021). roic_proxy and gross margin are null in fundamentals.json (the filer does not tag the needed lines), so the ROE series is the computed return evidence available. A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 3.20 vs 3-yr median 5.95 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.1x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Diversified infrastructure contractor with a record backlog but a weak 4/10 moat and volatile, working-capital-driven owner's earnings — at $190.70 it clears nothing: weighted IRR 7.7%, weighted IV@15% $73.76, and even the super-bull IV@15% ($144.66) sits below price; it would need ~$74 to clear 15%.
moat_for: Scale and national footprint — one of the few contractors that can execute large multi-region power, pipeline, clean-energy and communications programs
Record 18-month backlog of $21.4B at Q2 2026 (+30% YoY, ~1.2x book-to-bill) gives unusual revenue visibility for a contractor
Incumbency and long relationships with utilities, telecom carriers and energy customers; bonding and safety record gate large-project bidding
Diversified end markets (Power Delivery, Clean Energy & Infrastructure, Pipeline, Communications) plus data-center exposure via the July 2026 Superior Group acquisition
moat_against: Competitively bid, project-based work — no recurring revenue or durable pricing power; customers can and do re-bid
Returns at/below cost of capital through most of the cycle: ROE -1.8% to 12.9% over 2021-25, net margin 2.79% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json)
Labor- and fleet-intensive cost structure — wage pressure and execution on fixed-price projects flow straight to OE
Growth partly bought: serial acquisitions (Superior Group $1.65B, debt-financed, closed July 2026) add integration and leverage risk
Segment cyclicality — Communications softness (RDOF roll-off, wireline deferrals) and pipeline project timing whipsaw results
